correctness.rationale: Correctness PASS. For a=2/[b(1-b)] and x in (0,1), exact log-odds drift h(F_b(x))-h(x)=-a(x-b). A genuine two-cycle would have x+y=2b and a=integral_-1^1 h'(b+tz)dt >2h'(b)=2/[b(1-b)] by strict convexity, impossible. The classical no-period-two interval theorem gives convergence to 0,b,1, while the map's drift sign excludes endpoint limits from interior starts. Taylor coefficients F_b(b+y)-b=-y+C y³+D y⁴+E y⁵+O(y6), C=2(1-3B)/(3B²), E=2(30B²-20B+3)/(15B⁴), B=b(1-b); F²(b+y)-b=y-2Cy³+(3C²-2E)y⁵+O(y6). For even n=2j, reciprocal square u_j advances 4C+(6C²+4E)/u_j+O(u_j^-3/2). Since C>0, u_j=4Cj+O(log j); summable errors give u_j-4Cj-K log j->finite, K=(6C²+4E)/(4C). The next odd step increments reciprocal square by 2C+o(1), so the same full n-sequence constant exists. Explicit derivative makes exceptional landing preimages countable. Independent exact symbolic Taylor and K tests at b=1/5,3/10,1/2; not extrapolated finite sampling.
